description: Build, break, debug and evaluate in your own environment.

lessons.title: Lab: GPU memory & numerical formats
lessons.conceptOverview: Calculate weights-only memory for 7B and 70B parameters, then add an explicit optimizer-state budget. Compare host-to-device transfer time with compute time.
lessons.whyItMatters: Account for memory, communication and recovery.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Weights are only part of training memory: gradients, optimizer states, master weights, activations and temporary buffers also consume VRAM. A 70B model needs about 140 GB for two-byte weights alone, before runtime overhead. FP32, FP16, BF16 and FP8 trade range and precision; hardware and kernels determine usable support.

sections.title: 1. Establish a baseline
sections.content: Write down your inputs, expected behavior and constraints before starting. Calculate weights-only memory for 7B and 70B parameters, then add an explicit optimizer-state budget. Compare host-to-device transfer time with compute time.

sections.title: 2. Introduce a failure
sections.content: Test the mistaken assumption: A model that fits for inference necessarily fits for training. Record the observed result and the point where it diverges from your prediction.

sections.title: 3. Debug and evaluate
sections.content: Use the mechanism to explain the failure: Weights are only part of training memory: gradients, optimizer states, master weights, activations and temporary buffers also consume VRAM. A 70B model needs about 140 GB for two-byte weights alone, before runtime overhead. FP32, FP16, BF16 and FP8 trade range and precision; hardware and kernels determine usable support. Change one variable at a time. Repeat the baseline and add a held-out case. Submit the implementation, results and limitations.

commonMistakes: A model that fits for inference necessarily fits for training.
keyTakeaways: Weights are only part of training memory: gradients, optimizer states, master weights, activations and temporary buffers also consume VRAM.

lessons.title: Lab: Parallelism & communication
lessons.conceptOverview: Sketch placement of an eight-layer model across four GPUs using data, tensor and pipeline parallelism. Identify each communication boundary.
lessons.whyItMatters: Account for memory, communication and recovery.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: DDP replicates model state and all-reduces gradients. FSDP and ZeRO shard different combinations of parameters, gradients and optimizer state. Tensor parallelism splits operations, pipeline parallelism splits layers, and expert parallelism distributes MoE experts. NCCL provides GPU communication collectives; interconnect bandwidth can dominate multi-node runs.

lessons.title: Lab: Efficient and recoverable training
lessons.conceptOverview: Measure throughput, peak memory and GPU utilization for accumulation and checkpointing variants. Interrupt a run and verify that restoration resumes the intended data position.
lessons.whyItMatters: Account for memory, communication and recovery.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Gradient accumulation increases effective batch size without retaining every microbatch activation. Gradient checkpointing recomputes activations to save memory. DeepSpeed and Accelerate help orchestrate training, but do not eliminate configuration and profiling work. Durable checkpoints need optimizer, scheduler, data position and random-number state as well as weights.
